Lemma <REF_0001>
says that morphisms of schemes satisfy fpqc descent.
In other words, given a scheme <MATH_0001> and schemes <MATH_0002>, <MATH_0003> over <MATH_0004>
the functor
<MATH_0005>
satisfies the sheaf condition for the fpqc topology.
The simplest case of this is the following. Suppose that <MATH_0006>
is a surjective flat morphism of affines. Let <MATH_0007>
be a morphism of schemes over <MATH_0008> which is compatible with the
canonical descent data. Then there exists a unique morphism
<MATH_0009> whose base change to <MATH_0010> is <MATH_0011>. In fact this
special case follows in a straightforward manner from
Lemma <REF_0002>.
And, in turn, that lemma is a formal consequence of the following
two facts:
(a) the base change functor by a faithfully flat morphism is faithful, see
Lemma <REF_0003>
and (b) a scheme satisfies the sheaf condition for the fpqc topology, see
Lemma <REF_0004>.
